question.text: For conversion of compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>, the rate constant of the reaction was found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Lmol</mi><mmultiscripts><mo> </mo><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The order of the reaction is _____ .

solution.text:
Rate(r) =kAn

⇒k=rateAn

Unit of rate constant is related to order of reaction(n) by the relation: conc.1-ntime-1

Thus,
⇒Lmol-1⇒1-n=-1n=2
